source: MINESEC progression sheets 2026-27, English Sub System, General Education, Upper Sixth All (minesec-ige.com)

contenu: Lesson 1: Gravitation: Newton’s law inverse square and Kepler’s laws. Qualitative description of the earth’s gravitational field. Field Strength
Lesson 4: Variation of g inside and outside the earth. Gravitational potential and gravitational potential energy
Lesson 5: Escape velocity Orbital speed and geostationary satellites. Orbital speed and movement of satellites with geostationary satellites as example
Lesson 8: Motion in the gravitational field: Projectile motion (See Lower sixth mechanics)
Lesson 2: Waves: Definition, Classification base on mode of propagation and medium of propagation with specific examples. Characteristics of Waves.
Lesson 3: The progressive wave and equation. Graphical representation of waves.
Lesson 6: Waves Phenomena: Production, reflection, refraction, diffraction, Interference. Single slit pattern
Lesson 7: Double slits and multiple slits interference patterns and measurement of wavelength of a wave
Lesson 14: Doppler Effect for Sound in air with specific cases of moving source/ stationary observer and moving observer with stationary source.
Lesson 15: Stationary waves and characteristics
Lesson 9: Electric charge: Origin, types, and the basic law of electrostatics; Conductors and insulators; Charging; Point action and the lightening conductor
Lesson 12: Coulomb’s law and inverse square nature. Dependence of size of force on medium. Electric field and field strength
Lesson 10: Waves Phenomena: Polarization- definition and production of plane polarized waves
Lesson 11: The factors affecting the speed of transverse waves on taut strings and wires
Lesson 13: Electric potential and work done in moving a charge in an electric field. Electric field dipole and torque.
Lesson 16: Capacitors: Circuit symbols, identification of capacitors. Measurement of capacitance. Factors which affect capacitance. Relative permittivity
Lesson 17: Combination of capacitors (series & parallel) Energy/charge stored in a different combinations of capacitors connected to a dc power supply
Lesson 20: Charging and discharging capacitors through resistors and time constant. The equations for charging/ discharging and interpretations at t=0 and as t →∞.
Lesson 18: Measurement of the speed of sound in air.
Lesson 19: Electromagnetic waves and their characteristics. EM-spectrum; production, detection and uses of different sections
Lesson 21: X-rays, production and uses Meaning and application of plane polarized em waves.
Lesson 24: Light sources. Optical transmission grating with normal incidence
Lesson 25: Multiple slit diffraction. Reflection and refraction at plane interfaces
Lesson 28: Laws of refraction. Refractive index
Lesson 29: Dispersion. Total internal reflection and critical angle. Lenses: principal focus, focal length.

Lesson 32: Familiarity with practical situations in which a single converging lens produces a magnified or diminished image, dioptre. Prisms, optical instruments eg compound microscopes and Astronomical telescopes
Lesson 33: Conservation of energy for waves in free space from a point source. Inverse square law

Lesson 22: The magnetic field Magnetic flux density and its units (the tesla). Field patterns of current-carrying conductors (straight wire, plane circular coil, solenoid) Force on a current-carrying conductor in a uniform magnetic field. The direction of the force from Fleming’s left hand rule
Lesson 23: Forces on objects in cross-fields Torque on a rectangular coil within a uniform magnetic field (T = NAIB) The principle of the electric motor (dc and ac types)

Lesson 26: Biot-Savart law Ampere’s law Magnetic flux density within a long solenoid, long straight wire, and plane circular coil (B = µonI, B = µoI/2r, B = µoI /2πr). Force between two current-carrying conductors
Lesson 27: Force on a moving charge in uniform magnetic field Measurement of specific charge (e/mo) The Hall effect dia, para- and ferro-magnetic materials Magnetic Shielding The Lorentz force
Lesson 30: Faraday’s and Lenz’s laws of electromagnetic induction. Induced e.m.f. across a conductor moving with velocity v, through uniform magnetic field. Simple DC and AC generator principles.

Lesson 31: Meaning of self-inductance and mutual inductance. The L-R DC circuit (the growth and decay of current) Energy stored in an inductor Coefficient M and L should be understood to be defined as the constants in the equations: Nф = LI Nф2=MI1 and Nф1=MI2

Lesson 34: Theory of transformers Knowledge, understanding but not derivation of V_(p )/V_s =N_p/N_s =I_s/I_p for ideal transformers Sources of power losses for practical transformers and how each is minimized.
Lesson 35: Root-mean-square values Impedance and resonance use of f_0=1/(2π√LC)
Lesson 38: Power in a.c. Circuits. Rectification of ac signals and Smoothening
Lesson 36: Photoelectric effect. The photons, Plank constant
Lesson 37: Einstein’s photoelectric equation. Wave-particle duality
Lesson 39: The atom, Rutherford’s alpha scattering experiment and atomic model.
Lesson 40: Emission and absorption spectra. Energy levels. The electron volt.
Lesson 41: Use of equation: E=hf = E2 -E1. The Schrodinger model of the hydrogen atom
Lesson 42: Nuclear stability and radioactivity Properties of radiations and applications
Lesson 43: Mass defect in nuclear processes and relation to energy Nuclear fission and fusion
Lesson 45: Thermionic emission and the electron gun
Lesson 47: Semicoductors and doping The p-n junction diode, biasing and applications
Lesson 49: The transistor Logic gates and amplfiers
Lesson 44: Representing information: Analogue method, digital method, advantages and disadvantages. Radio waves: Surface or ground wave
Lesson 46: Sky wave, space wave. Aerials: transmitting, receiving aerials. Tuning circuit, its resonance curve
Lesson 48 Transmission of information: modulation, demodulation. Amplitude modulation (AM), frequency modulation (FM), advantages and disadvantages of each over the other
Lesson 50: Analogue and digital signals Analogue to Digital converters Digital to Analogue converters. Advantages of each over the other
Lesson 52: Communication Channels: Band width, and sidebands, Use of satellite for communication. Base station and their role
Lesson 51: The physics of vision and defects Hearing and defects
Lesson 53: Biological Measurements for the heart Imaging in medical diagnosis (Non-ionising methods)
Lesson 54: Ionizing technics in imaging for medical diagnosis Use of optical fibres in medical procedure
